summary.title: TBM 27/52: Mandate Levels
summary.one_liner: A nine-level "Mandate Levels" model for discussing autonomy, empowerment and agency in teams by describing how much authority a team or role has over the work.
takeaways: Autonomy, empowerment and agency can be made concrete by mapping work into nine mandate levels, from specific to general.
Use the model to start conversations about where teams and roles operate, not to grade or rank teams; it is explicitly not a maturity model.
Map roles on and off the team to expose rigid or messy boundaries, such as the gap between a team and the business.
Mandate level can apply to teams, individuals and individual pieces of work, and it can shift over the life of an effort.
You cannot fake a mandate by assigning OKRs a team does not control; avoid buzzwords and name the specific level instead.
summary.summary: The post introduces Mandate Levels, a nine-level model the author created to describe a sphere of authority and autonomy for work, ranging from very specific to very general. It shows several example diagrams comparing team operating boundaries, such as a rigid product owner and product manager setup versus a product-led trio with overlapping mandates. The author lists cautions: the model is not a maturity grade, work happens at all levels, and org constraints, experience and preferences limit how much mandate a team can take. The post ends with advice to name the specific level rather than use vague words like empowerment, and links a short explainer video and a Miro template.
